safety_talks.body: Before any work above 6 ft: inspect the ladder/lift, tie off, and clear the drop zone below. Nobody works overhead without a spotter.
safety_talks.title: Elevated work check

safety_talks.body: Read the SDS. Ventilate when tooling in enclosed spaces, skin protection for MEKP/primer, no open flame near solvents.
safety_talks.title: Sealant & solvents

safety_talks.body: Clear the drop zone, cap exposed screws, sweep glass shards immediately. A clean deck is a safe deck.
safety_talks.title: Housekeeping

safety_talks.body: Two people minimum over 150 lb. Carry lites on edge, never flat. Coated/tempered edges cut — gloves on, cups rated for the surface.
safety_talks.title: Glass handling

safety_talks.body: Inspect straps and cups before every pick. Nobody under a suspended unit. Set A-frames braced and loaded evenly.
safety_talks.title: Lift & rigging

safety_talks.body: On hot elevations rotate shade breaks, water every 20 min. Dark glass against sun cracks — and burns hands.
safety_talks.title: Heat & hydration

safety_talks.body: Three points of contact. Level the base. Scissor/boom lift: harness, gate closed, check the ground rating.
safety_talks.title: Ladders & lifts

tools.note: Rated 150 lb/cup on clean dry glass

tools.name: Anemometer
tools.note: Wind check before lifts above 1 story

howto_json.detail: Measure width at 3 points and height at 2; confirm the unit fits with 1/4-1/2" shim clearance before carrying it up.
howto_json.title: Dry-fit and check the rough opening

howto_json.detail: Last installs cammed out upper hinge screws — pre-drill to avoid it.
howto_json.title: Pre-drill the hinge side

howto_json.detail: Set it just outside before the lift; two-person set keeps the cladding clean.
howto_json.title: Stage the unit outside the opening

howto_json.detail: Plastic shims with an impact on clutch; check square with a diagonal tape before fastening.
howto_json.title: Shim and level

howto_json.detail: Flashing tape on the first pass; foam-seal clean. Watch fingers on tempered edges.
howto_json.title: Flash and seal

window_types.name: Casement 30x50
tips_json: Pre-check RO with diagonal tape before setting the unit
Stage the unit outside the opening before the lift
Use impact with clutch + plastic shims on casement hinges
Bring a Japanese pull saw when the RO is racked
Call out pinch points on the swing path
watch_outs_json: Upper hinge screws can cam out on casements
Out-of-square RO by 3/8" will blow the time estimate
Tempered edges — watch fingers

howto_json.detail: Width at 3 points, height at 2, both diagonals. A double-hung binds fast if the sill is not level — fix the opening, never force the frame.
howto_json.title: Verify the rough opening

howto_json.detail: Shim at the setting points only, snug not tight. The sill is where a hung window lives or dies.
howto_json.title: Set the sill dead level

howto_json.detail: Even reveal on all four sides before fastening. A tapered reveal tells you which corner is off.
howto_json.title: Set and check reveal

howto_json.detail: One over-driven screw racks the frame and drops the sashes. Check diagonals after each side.
howto_json.title: Fasten per schedule, re-check square

howto_json.detail: Laps shed downhill. Low-expansion foam in passes so the jambs do not bow and jam the balances.
howto_json.title: Flash jambs then head, foam light

window_types.name: Hopper 30x24
tips_json: Hopper opens inward at the top - confirm swing clearance inside before setting.
Drain side out; flash sides first, top flashing last over the flange lip.
Level first - a racked hopper will not seal at the sill.
Caulk flanges left/right/top, leave the bottom to drain.
Test the latch and full open/close before final caulk.
watch_outs_json: Common in basements/wells - verify the well drains so the unit does not sit in water.
Confirm setout depth (stucco vs rock).
Do not seal the bottom weep holes.

window_types.name: Double-Hung 32x52
tips_json: Drain slots on the bottom face OUT - confirm before lifting it in.
Flash the sides first, top flashing last over the flange lip.
Caulk flanges left/right/top, never the bottom - the bottom has to drain.
Level first, then center. Set the flange screws, then remove the shims.
Check both sashes slide before you screw off - a racked frame binds a double-hung fast.
watch_outs_json: Do not seal the bottom weep holes - a double-hung will pond water if you do.
Confirm stucco vs rock setout before install.
On hot days ease off screw torque on vinyl frames.

window_types.name: Slider 72x48
tips_json: Large slider - plan a 2-person lift with the suction machine; never solo it.
Level and square are everything - test-roll the panels before you commit screws.
Drain out; flash the sides, then top flashing last over the flange.
Shim to level, set flange screws, pull shims, re-check the roll.
Caulk flanges left/right/top only; leave the bottom open.
watch_outs_json: Heavy glass - keep everyone clear of the drop zone and the suction path.
A slightly racked large slider will not seal or roll - do not accept it.
Confirm the suction-cup machine is on site before scheduling this unit.

window_types.name: Picture 48x48
tips_json: Stationary unit - no moving parts, so the finish caulk is the whole quality story.
Drain side out; flash sides first, top flashing last over the flange lip.
Level and center - with no sash to hide it, an out-of-level picture window shows.
Exterior finish caulk is permanent: tape a ~3/4 in gap, caulk, then tool one smooth line.
Photograph the finished caulk line and that all tape/stickers are removed.
watch_outs_json: Sloppy tooling on the exterior caulk is the most common callback on picture windows.
Confirm setout depth (stucco vs rock).
Big glass = 2-person lift; keep clear of the drop zone.

window_types.name: Awning 30x24
tips_json: Drain side out; flash sides first, top flashing last over the flange.
Level matters - an awning that is off will not seal against the frame when cranked shut.
Caulk flanges left/right/top only; leave the bottom to drain.
Set flange screws after leveling, pull shims, then crank through full travel.
Confirm the arm hardware operates smoothly before final caulk.
watch_outs_json: An out-of-level awning leaks at the hinge side - level carefully.
Confirm setout depth up front.
Do not force vinyl on hot days.

window_types.name: Picture 60x48
tips_json: Stationary - the exterior caulk finish is the whole job quality; take your time tooling it.
2-person lift; set the bottom in, tilt up, drain side facing out.
Flash sides first, top flashing last over the flange lip.
Level and center; caulk flanges left/right/top, leave the bottom to drain.
Photograph the final caulk line and confirm tape/stickers removed.
watch_outs_json: Tooling quality varies by installer - a bumpy caulk line is a visible defect.
Confirm stucco vs rock setout.
Keep clear of suspended glass during the lift.

window_types.name: Slider 60x48
tips_json: This is a 2-person lift - use suction cups or straps. Set the bottom into the frame, then tilt up.
Get it dead level before screwing off or the panels will not roll smoothly.
Drain side out; flash sides first, top flashing last over the flange lip.
Caulk flanges left/right/top, leave the bottom to drain.
Roll both panels full travel before final caulk to confirm no bind.
watch_outs_json: A racked slider binds - level and square matter more here than on a small window.
Never get under a suspended panel during the lift.
Confirm stucco vs rock setout before setting depth.

window_types.name: Single-Hung 32x52
tips_json: Find the drain slots on the bottom of the frame - that side faces OUT. Never set it drain-side in.
Flash both sides before you set the window; roll the TOP flashing last, over the flange lip, so water sheds down.
Caulk the flanges left, right and top only - leave the bottom open so trapped water can drain.
Shim and level first, center second. Level always wins. Set screws through the flanges, then pull the shims.
St. George standard: caulk off the top and side weep holes, leave the bottom drains open.
watch_outs_json: Out-of-level wall: shim to true level even if the reveal looks uneven - flag the foreman if it is more than ~1 in off.
Confirm stucco vs rock before setting depth - it changes the setout ~1 in (rock) vs ~1.5 in (stucco).
Vinyl softens in high heat - do not overdrive screws or force a bind on hot days.

window_types.name: Casement 30x48
tips_json: Drain side faces OUT. Flash sides before setting, top flashing last over the flange.
Level is critical on a casement - if it is out, the sash will not seal or will swing on its own.
Caulk flanges left/right/top only; leave the bottom for drainage.
Set screws through the flange after leveling, then pull the shims and check the sash swings clean.
Test the crank through full travel before you finish caulk.
watch_outs_json: A casement that is not dead level will not latch - do not rush the level step.
Confirm setout depth (stucco vs rock) up front.
Watch the sash edge for scratches when unpackaging with a utility knife.

howto_json.detail: A large picture unit is heavy and often tempered/laminated. Check the etched bug and recalc crew/lift gear before it comes up.
howto_json.title: Confirm glass spec and safety bug

howto_json.detail: Set on edge, never flat — a fixed lite this size will pop its IGU seal if racked during handling.
howto_json.title: Dry-fit and stage on A-frames

howto_json.detail: Setting blocks at the quarter points carry the weight. Center the unit so the perimeter joint is uniform for backer rod.
howto_json.title: Set on blocks, center the reveal

howto_json.detail: Fixed units still rack. Fasten progressively and keep diagonals equal; a racked picture unit shows as a wavy reflection.
howto_json.title: Anchor without racking

howto_json.detail: Rod to half the joint width, tool the same day. Big lites move a lot thermally — the joint must stretch, not shear.
howto_json.title: Backer rod + tooled sealant

window_types.name: Bay 72x48
tips_json: Bay is a structural, 3-person unit - it needs support below and cable/knee bracing above per plan.
Confirm the head board and support brackets are in before you hang any weight.
Flash the full perimeter carefully; the roof/seat connections are the leak risk, not just the flanges.
Level and center the center lite first, then bring the flankers to it.
Seal the seat and roof junctions and photograph every flashing/caulk joint.
watch_outs_json: Bays fail from under-support and roof-junction leaks - never skip the bracing or seat flashing.
3-person job with heavy glass - stage the lift and keep the drop zone clear.
Confirm the opening framing and setout with the foreman before starting - bays are non-starters if the rough opening is wrong.
